Deployment guide

Cloudflare Pages, without guesswork.

Short version: Deployment settings depend on whether a repository is plain HTML, Worker code, or a framework that produces a build directory. This repository builds one static dist/ directory and deploys that output.

Three project shapes

Plain HTML

Root files such as index.html, CSS, JavaScript, and assets need no framework build. Deploy the root or the exact public folder that contains the HTML.

Worker code

Worker projects have a runtime entry point such as src/index.js, a package manifest, and usually a Wrangler configuration.

Framework build

Vite, React static export, Astro, and Hugo produce an output directory such as dist, build, or public.

This repository

The source site lives in site/. The build creates a clean dist/ directory so stale files do not survive a deployment. The recommended setup is:

Build command: bash scripts/build-site.sh .
Deploy command: npx wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name actions-budget-policy
Root directory: /
Production branch: main

Before deploying

  • Confirm site/index.html becomes dist/index.html.
  • Keep CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID in secrets.
  • Verify _headers and _redirects are in the output.
  • Confirm every redirect has an HTML fallback.
  • Run bash scripts/build-site.sh . and bash scripts/validate-html.sh dist.

GitHub Pages parity

GitHub Pages consumes the same generated directory through its Pages artifact workflow. Edit site/, build once, and keep both hosts aligned.
